title: .NET HttpClient · Connection pooling
excerpt: Each HttpClient instance uses a connection pool owned by its underlying SocketsHttpHandler. Disposing the client disposes its pool, so creating and disposing a client for each request can create unnecessary connections and exhaust available TCP ports. Reuse clients or allow IHttpClientFactory to pool the handlers.
terms: HttpClient 连接池 连接复用 套接字 端口耗尽 socket exhaustion

title: .NET HttpClient · DNS changes
excerpt: HttpClient resolves DNS when it creates a connection. It does not track DNS time-to-live values. Configure SocketsHttpHandler.PooledConnectionLifetime if the application needs to pick up DNS changes. When the lifetime expires and the connection finishes its current request, the connection is closed and the next new connection performs DNS resolution.
terms: HttpClient DNS 解析 缓存 连接寿命 生命周期 PooledConnectionLifetime

title: .NET HttpClient · Client lifetime
excerpt: The recommended choices include long-lived HttpClient instances with PooledConnectionLifetime configured, or short-lived clients created by IHttpClientFactory. The factory pools HttpMessageHandler instances so a newly created client can reuse an existing handler and connection pool.
terms: HttpClient 工厂 长连接 短生命周期 复用 IHttpClientFactory

title: ASP.NET Core · Minimal API routes
excerpt: ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs can use MapGroup to organize endpoints that share a route prefix. A route group can apply endpoint conventions as a group, for example RequireAuthorization or shared metadata. Individual route handlers can still declare their own route patterns.
terms: ASP.NET Core 最小 API 路由 分组 授权 MapGroup RequireAuthorization

title: Go · Context cancellation
excerpt: WithCancel returns a derived Context with a Done channel. Its Done channel closes when its cancel function is called or when the parent context is canceled. Calling the cancel function releases resources associated with the derived context.
